code.reason: Revert experiment 5's mixed far-target/full-range training sampler because it did not preserve broad-task competence on either the research or held-out task-reference panel; restore the experiment-5 code parent.

last_lineage_decision.reason: Keep the accepted champion at 97.0%: both experiment-5 checkpoints reached only 55.5% with 89 truncated failures, while the champion reached 97.0% with 6 failures. Paired outcomes favored the champion by 85-2 and 87-4, and the task-reference result was 55.0% versus 98.0%.

evaluation_plan.question: Does adding target-polar observation features recover the previously hard angular sector and improve broad full-range reach-and-hold performance over the accepted champion?
evaluation_plan.reason: Training reward rises sharply at the late checkpoints, but training success remains zero and reward is not task success. Measuring checkpoints 110592 and 120832 plus the champion on the identical 200-episode research panel provides overall success and per-episode angular and failure diagnostics, while the task-reference panel for checkpoint 120832 and the champion tests whether any improvement generalizes to held-out targets. Paired comparisons isolate the intervention from panel variation.

result.change: Append normalized target radius and sine/cosine target angle to the existing observation. The plausible alternative is that the remaining failures are caused by control or optimization limits rather than target representation; the fixed full-range 200-episode evaluation, together with its per-episode angular diagnostics, distinguishes these explanations by testing both overall success and recovery of the previously concentrated hard sector.
result.hypothesis: Adding smooth target polar features to the observation while retaining the successful 14-20 cm training curriculum will raise full-range success from 97% to at least 98% by improving generalization in the -160 to -100 degree sector without sacrificing the rest of the task.
